title: Air-fryer mackerel fillets
subtitle: Mackerel fillets with crisp skin cooked in the air fryer in under 10 minutes.
excerpt: Fresh mackerel fillets air-fried skin-side down until the skin crisps and the flesh is opaque. Seasoned simply with salt, pepper, and lemon. Ready in 8 minutes. Serves two.
sourceNotes: Mackerel is an oily fish widely caught in British and Atlantic waters. Fresh mackerel benefits from dry, high heat which crisps the skin while the natural oil in the flesh keeps it moist. The air fryer suits it particularly well.

content.text: Mackerel fillets cook fast and forgive little overcooking: a minute too long and the flesh dries out. At 200°C in the air fryer, two fillets take 8 minutes. Cook skin-side down for the first 6 minutes and the skin crisps while the flesh cooks through from the heat of the basket floor. A brief flip for the last 2 minutes finishes the top.

Pat the {{mackerel-fillets}} mackerel fillets dry. Brush the skin side with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil and season both sides with {{sea-salt-flakes}} of flaked salt and cracked black pepper. Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Place fillets skin-side down. Cook for 6 minutes without disturbing, then flip carefully and cook for a further 1-2 minutes until the flesh is opaque throughout. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

items.cause: Skin was wet before cooking, or basket not hot enough.
items.fix: Pat the skin side completely dry before oiling. Preheat the air fryer fully before adding the fillets.
Wait the full 6 minutes skin-side down. The fillet releases cleanly from the basket once the skin is fully crisped. If it sticks, give it another minute.
Mackerel needs only 8 minutes in total. The flesh is done when it has turned from translucent to opaque. Remove immediately.

content.text: Air-fryer mackerel fillets are one of the fastest fresh-fish meals possible. Good with a green salad, crusty bread, or new potatoes. The same method works for salmon fillets or trout, with 10-12 minutes total for a thicker piece.
